subject: general
question: Who sacrificed her life along with 363 others in 1731 to protect the Khejri trees in Rajasthan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrita Devi Bishnoi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The historic sacrifice for environmental conservation took place in **September 1731** in the village of **Khejarli**, located in the **Jodhpur** district of **Rajasthan**.
 
• **Amrita Devi Bishnoi**, along with her **three daughters**, stood against the soldiers of **Maharaja Abhai Singh** of **Marwar**, who were sent to cut **Khejri trees** to fuel lime kilns for the construction of a new palace.
 
• During this protest, **Amrita Devi** famously declared that if a tree could be saved at the cost of one's head, it was still a cheap price to pay. She was the first to be martyred while hugging a tree to protect it.
 
• Following her example, a total of **363** members of the **Bishnoi community** from **84 villages** sacrificed their lives to save the sacred trees. ***Hence, the statement regarding Amrita Devi Bishnoi is correct.***
 
• This event is recognized as a pioneering movement in environmentalism and served as a major inspiration for the modern **Chipko Movement** led by Sunderlal Bahuguna in the **1970s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Medha Patkar**:
 
 
• She is a prominent Indian social activist known for her leading role in the **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (NBA).
 
• The movement was started in **1985** to protest against the construction of large dams across the **Narmada River**, particularly the **Sardar Sarovar Dam**, due to the displacement of local tribal communities and environmental damage.
 
 
 
• **Vandana Shiva**:
 
 
• She is an world-renowned environmentalist and eco-feminist based in **Delhi**.
 
• She founded **Navdanya** in **1987**, an organization dedicated to biodiversity conservation, organic farming, and the rights of farmers to save and share seeds.
 
 
 
• **Sunita Narain**:
 
 
• She is a distinguished Indian environmentalist who serves as the **Director General** of the **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)**.
 
• She has been a vocal advocate for sustainable development and was named in **Time Magazine’s** list of **100 Most Influential People** in **2016**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Khejri Tree (Prosopis cineraria)**:
 
 
• It was declared the **State Tree of Rajasthan** in **1983**.
 
• Known as the "Golden Tree of the Desert" or "Ghaf," it plays a vital role in the ecosystem of the **Thar Desert** by preventing soil erosion and providing fodder (Loom) and food (Sangri).
 
 
 
• **Bishnoi Community**:
 
 
• The sect was founded by **Guru Jambheshwar** (also known as Jambhoji) in **1485**.
 
• The community follows **29 tenets** (Bish-noi), which include a strict prohibition against cutting green trees and killing animals, making them some of the world's first organized environmentalists.
 
 
 
• **Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award**:
 
 
• The **Government of India** and the **Rajasthan Government** instituted this national award to honor individuals and communities for their extraordinary courage and dedication to protecting **wildlife** and **forests**.
 
• A commemorative fair (Mela) is held every year on **Bhadrapad Shukla Dashmi** at **Khejarli** village to pay tribute to the martyrs.
